title: 01 · Incident response — first 2 minutes
description: What is burning, where it started, which racks and tenants are hit: one screen for the first two minutes.

panels.title: Pages firing
panels.description: Page-severity alerts firing in vmalert, before Alertmanager groups and inhibits them. 0 is the normal state.

panels.title: Notifications sent
panels.description: Alerts Alertmanager is routing to receivers now. At rest this is 1: the Watchdog heartbeat, a dead man's switch proving the alerting path works.

panels.title: Suppressed as consequences
panels.description: Alerts inhibited along the dependency chains (UPS → RPP → rack → node → GPU; CRAH → throttling; flapping link → its error counters). Many here and few notifications = people get the cause, not the noise.

panels.title: Tenants burning SLO
panels.description: Tenants spending their GPU-availability error budget faster than it accrues (burn rate > 1 over the last minute). The page fires at 14.4x on two windows.

panels.title: GPUs unavailable to tenants
panels.description: GPUs allocated to tenants minus GPUs that are usable (node Ready, no XID 79): the customer-facing blast radius.

panels.title: Nodes with no GPU telemetry
panels.description: 'Unknown' is not 'healthy': servers in the inventory whose GPU exporter went silent (unpowered, crashed, unreachable). A silent server must never look green.

targets.expr: count(node_topology_info unless on(Hostname) DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP) or vector(0)

panels.title: Dependency graph — the cause and the blast radius
panels.description: One dependency graph, live: power (UPS → row power panel → rack feed), cooling (CRAH → rack) and placement (rack → tenant). Colour is the state now. The first red or orange node whose parents are all green is the cause; everything coloured below it is the blast radius. Yellow is a precursor. Click a node for the reason. Computed at query time from the *_info join-table metrics: no topology labels on GPU series.

options.content:
**The first two minutes**

1. **Top row**: is anyone paged, how much was suppressed as a consequence, how many tenant GPUs are gone.
2. **Graph**, top down: the first red or orange node whose parents are all green is the cause; everything coloured below it is the blast radius. All power and cooling green, one rack orange: look at the fabric dashboard. **Yellow** is a precursor: working, but one failure away from red.
3. **Timeline** below: which layer turned red first.
4. **Alerts table**: owner and runbook of everything firing.

Then drill down: click a rack under *Where*.

panels.title: Where did it start — status by layer
panels.description: One line per layer, red while any signal of that layer is out of range. The first line to turn red is usually where the incident started: facilities first means the building, compute alone means the GPU.

panels.title: What is burning — firing alerts
panels.description: Every firing alert with owner (team), severity and location labels. Inhibited alerts are listed too; Alertmanager decides who is actually paged.

panels.title: Where — racks by worst signal (click for drill-down)
panels.description: Number of hurting signals per rack: hot inlet, throttling GPUs, one feed, no power, NotReady servers. Click a rack to open its facilities or GPU view.

panels.title: Who is hit — tenant GPU availability
panels.description: Share of each tenant's allocated GPUs that are usable now. Green at or above the 99.5% SLO target.

panels.title: Walk up the power chain — NotReady nodes and their upstream devices
panels.description: Each NotReady server with both of its power paths (PDU → RPP → UPS for feeds A and B) from the topology join. A device shared by every row is the common cause.

targets.expr: label_replace(kube_node_status_ready == 0, "Hostname", "$1", "node", "(.*)") * on(Hostname) group_left(rack, pdu_a, rpp_a, ups_a, pdu_b, rpp_b, ups_b) node_power_info

panels.title: Upstream power devices with no output
panels.description: UPS units and row power panels whose output is off. Any entry here is a facilities incident for a whole feed or row.

panels.title: Throttling GPUs by CRAH (cooling chain)
panels.description: Throttling GPUs grouped by the CRAH that cools them. Many under one CRAH = a cooling problem, not a GPU problem.

targets.expr: count by (crah) ((DCGM_FI_DEV_CLOCK_THROTTLE_REASONS > 0) * on(Hostname) group_left(crah) node_topology_info) or max by (crah) (node_topology_info) * 0

panels.title: Tenant training step time
panels.description: Seconds per training step per tenant job (baseline about 1.2 s). Throttling or a degraded link shows up here as a customer-visible slowdown; the ticket fires above 1.45 s.

panels.title: Tenant SLO burn rate (fast-burn page at 14.4x)
panels.description: How many times faster than allowed each tenant spends its error budget, on two windows (compressed to 1m/5m for the demo). The page needs both above 14.4x: fast enough to matter, sustained enough not to flap.

panels.title: Event log — warning and above, all layers
panels.description: Events from every layer at warning and above (VictoriaLogs): breaker trips, XID lines, link flaps, UPS alarms. Use it to confirm the order the timeline suggests.
